prompt: A solenoid 0.5 m long has 1000 turns and carries 3 A current. Find the energy stored in it (area = 0.001 m^2).
explanation: Two formulas, in order. The inductance of a solenoid is L = mu-nought N^2 A / l = (4 pi x 10^-7 x 1000^2 x 0.001) / 0.5. Take it in pieces: 1000^2 = 10^6, and 10^6 x 0.001 = 1000, so the top is 4 pi x 10^-7 x 1000 = 1.2566 x 10^-3, and dividing by 0.5 doubles it to L = 2.513 x 10^-3 H. Then the energy, U = 1/2 L I^2 = 0.5 x 2.513 x 10^-3 x 9 = 1.13 x 10^-2 J, which is 0.0113 J. Note that N is SQUARED in the inductance while I is squared in the energy, so both squares have to survive.

why.b: No. 4.5 J is 1/2 x 1 x 3^2, which is the energy formula with L taken as 1 H, so the inductance was never worked out.
why.c: No. 0.00251 J is the inductance 2.513 x 10^-3 with a J written after it. An inductance in henries is not an energy in joules.
why.d: No. 11.3 J is the right digits three powers of ten too large, which is what dropping the 0.001 m^2 area does.
why.e: No. 0.0226 J is twice the answer, which is what forgetting the half in 1/2 L I^2 gives.
